title: Naval on honesty, founder selection, habits and acceptance (Tim Ferriss Show, Naval half)
summary: In the first half of this Tim Ferriss combo episode, Naval explains why honesty and presence are core values, what he screens for in founders (intelligence, energy, integrity), and how he builds skills and habits instead of chasing epiphanies. He also covers reading old source books, choiceless-awareness meditation, and desire as a contract for unhappiness. The second half is Nick Kokonas and is excluded.

principles.text: Back founders with intelligence, energy and integrity; smart and energetic without integrity gives you a hardworking crook.
principles.quote: if you have someone who's high intelligence and high energy but a low Integrity what you've got is a hardworking smart Crook

principles.text: Integrity is what you do despite the money; a founder who treats others unfairly to please you will do it to you too.
principles.quote: if being ethical was profitable everybody would do it so what you're looking for is a core sense of values that rises above and beyond the pure Financial incentives

principles.text: Only invest in or work with people you genuinely like; your scarce time and mental energy matter more than money.
principles.quote: no amount of money is worth it you and I will both die with money in the bank it's not about money at this point

principles.text: Skills like investing, happiness and self-awareness are built over decades with feedback loops, not through a single epiphany.
principles.quote: I don't believe in the Epiphany theory of self-development where you read some book you have an incredible Epiphany

principles.text: For old problems, read old source books; time-filtered ideas are more likely correct than modern summaries.
principles.quote: when you're talking about solving old problems the older the problem the older the solution

principles.text: Desire is a contract to be unhappy until you get what you want, so choose desires carefully and keep big ones to a minimum.
principles.quote: desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want
